story: Osmar creates systems and processes that automate complex work and scale delivery. His career spans financial automation, business intelligence, data platforms and enterprise AI. Today, he builds AI-native teams through agents, reusable skills, shared knowledge and distributed execution. He founded Elygent, an independent AI platform company, and leads its product and platform architecture.

projects.name: Agent Factory

VCA Brain shares business memory, and an AI Loop turns recurring work into reusable skills and runtime recommendations. Use VCA Brain to share project context and observations so teams build on collective knowledge.

Bring people and agents together in Buzz; retain checkpointed state, independent validation and human review.

aiFactoryApproach: An AI factory is infrastructure purpose-built to produce intelligence, integrating compute and AI software for training and inference. Osmar uses the term for the transition from general data-center capacity to AI compute that serves the business. His stated contribution is the orchestration and application layer: connecting on-premises, local, remote and cloud execution to agents, reusable workflows and shared business knowledge. Agent Factory is his named enablement platform, not a synonym for ownership of an entire physical AI factory. GPU-fleet, facilities, power/cooling and procurement ownership are not established.

capabilities.title: AI Loop and reusable skills
capabilities.text: Converted business workflows into reusable agent skills. The AI Loop learns recurring user patterns, creates and improves skills from collective knowledge, and recommends them at runtime to increase reuse, standardization and adoption. Platform capability grows through shared skills and knowledge; this does not establish model-weight training or unrestricted self-modifying production code.

capabilities.title: V Agent: one way to delegate
capabilities.text: Built V Agent, Visa’s super agent; V stands for Visa. It packages agents and connects deployed platforms, surfaces and tools through one simplification layer. It orchestrates across Buzz, Paperclip, cloud agents and OpenClaw assistant instances, giving business users one simple way to delegate without managing the underlying systems. This definition was explicitly corrected by Osmar on September 10, 2026.

capabilities.title: VCA Brain: shared business memory
capabilities.text: Created VCA Brain to share project context, observations and collective knowledge across people using Agent Factory. Teams and agents can discover prior work, understand what colleagues are working on and reuse learning instead of starting from zero. VCA Brain is Visa work; do not equate it with the independent Elygent GBrain deployment or imply public access to Visa knowledge.

capabilities.title: Local, remote and cloud execution
capabilities.text: Centralized orchestration on premises while connecting local, remote and cloud compute. Users can delegate agentic work to Windows VDIs, local or remote machines, and cloud agents. This is orchestration and application-delivery work across enterprise compute, not evidence of owning GPU fleets, datacenter facilities or hardware procurement.

capabilities.title: Buzz: people and agents together
capabilities.text: Deployed Buzz as an agentic collaboration workspace, described by Osmar as agentic Slack, bringing humans and agents into one interface and connecting conversations to delegated desktop and cloud work. Buzz is a separate product, not an assertion that Slack itself was built or owned by Osmar. The Visa deployment is distinct from the native Buzz public demonstration.

capabilities.title: Agents that work for hours and days
capabilities.text: Set up and operationalized long-running agents that execute for hours and days toward business objectives, with checkpointed state, isolated contexts, independent validation and human review. No completion-rate benchmark or guarantee of uninterrupted execution was provided.

approach.label: Explore
approach.body: I follow new models, tools, and interaction patterns closely, looking for a concrete problem they can solve for the team.

approach.label: Evaluate
approach.body: Compare quality, reliability, latency, resource use and cost per useful result. The strongest tool depends on the workload and operating constraints.

approach.label: Package
approach.body: Bring the useful part into a reusable skill, tool, workflow, or platform feature with an owner and a clear boundary.

approach.label: Enable
approach.body: Make the capability accessible through familiar interfaces, hands-on guidance, and examples people can apply immediately.

approach.label: Improve
approach.body: Use feedback and operational evidence to refine the workflow, retain a reusable lesson, or retire what no longer helps.

frontierAgenda.status: Community-shared compute means hosting an open-weight model on contributed hardware and making inference available to authorized community members through Buzz. This is Osmar’s target for his community. Open-source agent software and locally hosted model weights are separate layers. A Grok-backed cloud demo must be labeled Grok; it is not evidence of self-hosted GLM, Kimi or another local model. A deployed Elygent local compute pool has not been established.
Exploring how business entities, relationships and actions can provide shared context for AI workflows. This is a research interest; a deployed digital twin or Palantir implementation is not claimed.
Knowledge relationships and scoped agent-guided retrieval are part of the platform approach. A deployed GraphRAG engine or quality benchmark is not claimed.
Working independent platform and bounded public demonstration
Experimental public lab; no payment-network integration or production commerce claim
Continued evaluation work; integration/security checks are not a statistical quality benchmark
